claims.statement: The `common` package centralizes cross-agent contracts for typed settings, task-to-model construction, temporary LangSmith configuration, and SSE serialization; P0 consumes these contracts in its FastAPI completion endpoint.

`Settings` is a Pydantic settings model that loads a UTF-8 root `.env`, reads case-insensitively, ignores extra keys, and supplies defaults for provider credentials, LangSmith, PostgreSQL, and Qdrant configuration.

`get_settings()` is a one-entry LRU-cached settings accessor, and `settings` is initialized from that accessor, so environment overrides require `get_settings.cache_clear()` before a new accessor result can reflect them.
`Settings.project_name(slug)` composes LangSmith projects as `<langsmith_project_prefix>/<slug>`, with `LearnAgenticAI` as the default prefix.
The root environment template documents the provider and LangSmith variable names expected by the shared settings contract.

`get_model()` routes `reasoning`, `tools`, `local`, `judge`, and `cheap` to the configured DeepSeek, GPT-4o, Ollama, Claude Opus, and GPT-4o-mini model IDs respectively; unknown task strings fall back to the reasoning route in both model construction and `model_id_for()`.

The `local` route constructs an OpenAI-compatible `ChatOpenAI` client for `https://ollama.com/v1` using `OLLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY`, while every other route uses OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible API and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`.
Model construction fails early with a `RuntimeError` naming the missing route-specific credential: `OLLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY` for local routing and `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` for all OpenRouter-routed tasks.
Every client returned by `get_model()` has temperature zero, two retries, and a caller-controlled `max_tokens` cap whose default is 1024.
The project's verification record identifies the explicit `max_tokens=1024` default as the mitigation for an OpenRouter 402 caused by its assumed full output budget.

`setup(slug)` resolves settings on context entry, derives the prefixed project, snapshots four LangSmith environment variables, applies tracing/endpoint/project values and a nonempty API key for the block, and restores or removes each previous value in `finally`.

`current_project()` reports the currently set `LANGSMITH_PROJECT` value or `None`; tracing tests verify prefixed project selection, custom prefix use, and restoration of preexisting values after the scope exits.

Because `setup()` mutates process `os.environ`, its LangSmith selection is process-global rather than request-local; it should scope the actual operation narrowly and cannot independently isolate simultaneous differently configured requests.
P0 opens `setup("P0-smoke")` around its async agent stream and converts any exception from that scope into an SSE `error` event with code `agent_exception`.
`ui_bridge` defines a closed six-event SSE vocabulary—`token`, `tool_start`, `tool_end`, `message_end`, `error`, and `trace_meta`—and `to_sse()` rejects unknown event names with `ValueError`.

`to_sse()` returns UTF-8 SSE bytes in `event: <type>
data: <compact JSON>

` framing, using JSON serialization with compact separators and non-ASCII preservation.

The shared event helpers fix the backend payload shapes: token content; tool start name/arguments/call ID; tool end call ID/result; message end finish reason; error message/code; and trace metadata run URL/run ID.
P0 streams every nonempty LangChain chunk as a `token` event, then emits `message_end("stop")` followed by `trace_meta` containing its request run ID and LangSmith URL.
The chat UI mirrors the six-event vocabulary in its TypeScript union and parser guard, incrementally parses backend SSE lines, and discards malformed JSON or unknown event names.
The chat UI appends token content, correlates tool results only to an existing call ID, attaches trace metadata, and renders stream errors inline in the pending assistant message.

The UI posts `{ messages, stream: true }` to `/v1/chat/completions`, whose `/v1/*` path is rewritten to `NEXT_PUBLIC_AGENT_BASE_URL` with a localhost:8000 default; P0 validates nonempty messages, maps supported roles to LangChain messages, creates a UUID run ID, and returns a `text/event-stream` response.

Shared contract tests are offline and cover settings, model routing and missing credentials, tracing scope restoration, and SSE framing/payloads; provider-dependent P0 stream, invocation, and endpoint tests are marked `eval`, which the repository defines for LLM API calls.
